tiers.description: Claim is covered by deterministic fixtures, source references, multi-anchor support, and reviewer-facing limitations strong enough for bounded screening release review.
minimum_conditions: Claim is covered by the governed scientific-claim coverage manifest.
Claim has source references, methods-basis lines, and reference-case lines.
Mandatory reference-family claims meet the multi-anchor, multi-tier, multi-official-source bar.
No row claims field validation, calibration adequacy, regulatory acceptance, or source-engine equivalence.
boundary_lines: Reviewer-grade screening is still screening evidence, not regulator acceptance.
This tier does not imply site calibration, field validation, hydrology routing, fugacity Level III realism, or endpoint risk adequacy.
tiers.next_action_template: Maintain dual-source references, deterministic fixtures, generated worksheet artifacts, and non-author review on each release.

tiers.description: Claim is covered and source-backed, but remains experimental, challenge-path, or otherwise below the reviewer-grade reference anchor bar.
minimum_conditions: Claim is covered by at least one governed support fixture.
Claim has source references or official-source grounding.
Limitations and next corroboration actions are explicit.
Experimental families remain non-default and non-promoted.
boundary_lines: Source-grounded screening is corroboration, not field validation or calibration evidence.
Experimental model families require stronger independent benchmarks before promotion.
tiers.next_action_template: Add redistributable worked examples, independent benchmark references, and reviewer worksheets before considering promotion.

tiers.description: Claim is internally reproducible or normalization-parity checked, but external scientific corroboration is limited or intentionally out of scope.
minimum_conditions: Deterministic internal fixture or normalization-parity support exists.
External model/source-engine equivalence is not claimed.
The row identifies the missing external corroboration path.
boundary_lines: Internal oracles verify repo behavior, not external model correctness.
Adapter normalization parity does not validate upstream source-engine calculations.
tiers.next_action_template: Add independent source-grounded examples or external-engine comparison cases before increasing trust tier.

tiers.description: Evidence is useful for reviewer orientation, workflow QA, or expected classification checks, but it is explicitly synthetic.
minimum_conditions: Synthetic-demo status is explicit in the governed artifact.
No field-validation, calibration, regulatory-acceptance, or source-engine-equivalence claim is made.
boundary_lines: Synthetic demos are not empirical validation datasets.
Synthetic demos should not be used as evidence of scientific adequacy beyond workflow behavior.
tiers.next_action_template: Keep synthetic demos separated from benchmark and field-evidence packs; add real redistributable data only through a separate governed evidence layer.

tiers.description: Capability is intentionally deferred, unsupported by claim-level evidence, or present only as a boundary/documentation lane.
minimum_conditions: The gap or deferred boundary is explicit.
The row avoids decision-facing scientific claims.
The next action is concrete enough for a future release plan.
boundary_lines: Deferred rows are not failures when they are honest and fail closed.
Deferred rows must not be presented as validated model capability.
tiers.next_action_template: Define the missing evidence, validation, or implementation tranche before treating this row as usable scientific capability.

limitations: This rubric grades evidence posture for bounded screening release review only.
It does not establish regulator acceptance, field validation, source-engine equivalence, calibration adequacy, or full multimedia fate realism.

Rows may legitimately remain deferred when the public release intentionally excludes hydrology generation, GIS/catchment routing, WEPP/SWAT/PRZM execution, calibration, Level III transfer, or endpoint risk decisions.
